_comment: Logins listed in 'trusted' may have their bridge-report issues AUTO-PROCESSED: fetched,
sanitised, replayed against a scratch editor, fixed and committed without a human in the loop.
Everything else is labelled and left alone. This list is the security boundary of the whole
autonomous loop - schema validation catches mistakes, this catches adversaries.
EMPTY BY DEFAULT AND ON PURPOSE. A missing or malformed file also means nobody is trusted, so
the loop fails closed. Add a login only when you know it belongs to the person you think it does
- a GitHub login is not proof of identity by itself, and this grants that account the ability to
make this machine run editor operations unattended.
_who: 631Brando           - Brando, author of the DDS2 SDK this plugin builds against.
infectedcoolpat-jpg - Infected, the QOLCrafting_P mod team.
Both logins were confirmed to EXIST on GitHub before being added. That is the limit of what can be
verified from here: a login existing does not prove it belongs to the person Andre talks to.
2026-08-26: 'theinfector' was briefly trusted here in error - Andre gave that login, then corrected
it. It is an unrelated real account and it is REMOVED. Nothing was ever processed under it (no
bridge-report issues existed at any point while it was listed), but the lesson stands: a wrong login
in this file does not fail closed, it grants a stranger the ability to make this machine run editor
operations unattended. Confirm the handle against the person, not just against GitHub.
